orientation: Touches money (round.ts), which affects checkout via orderTotal. The risky one is money: roundToCents changes how exact half-cent ties round (away-from-zero to even), affecting 2 in-repo callers and 1 external consumer (invoice-service), with no tests covering it.

nodes.label: money
nodes.summary: Shared price-rounding helpers. roundToCents now rounds exact half-cent ties to the nearest even cent (banker's rounding) instead of always away from zero, to avoid cumulative upward drift when summing many rounded prices.

risk.why: Changes the tie-breaking rule for every rounded price; 2 in-repo callers and 1 external consumer (invoice-service) depend on it, and no tests exercise the new tie case.

nodes.label: roundToCents
nodes.summary: Rounds an amount to whole cents. Previously used Math.round (ties away from zero); now detects an exact .5-cent tie via a floating-point tolerance check and rounds that case to the even cent, otherwise falls back to Math.round as before.

risk.why: Exact-tie amounts now round differently (e.g. $0.005 rounds down instead of up); 2 in-repo callers and 1 external consumer, untested.

nodes.label: formatCents
nodes.summary: Formats an amount as a fixed two-decimal string by delegating to roundToCents. Unchanged itself, but its output for exact-tie inputs changes because it calls roundToCents, and it has an external consumer that will see the new behaviour.

risk.why: Inherits roundToCents' new tie behaviour; 1 external consumer (storefront-web) formats tie amounts differently with no test coverage.

nodes.label: checkout
nodes.summary: Computes order totals including tax, rounding once at the end via roundToCents. Included because orderTotal's output shifts for any order whose taxed subtotal lands exactly on a half-cent.

risk.why: orderTotal's rounded result can change for exact half-cent taxed subtotals, with no tests to catch a regression.

nodes.label: orderTotal
nodes.summary: Sums line items by price*qty, applies tax, then rounds once via roundToCents. Shown as context because it's the clearest in-repo caller whose final total can shift under the new tie-breaking rule.

risk.why: Relies entirely on roundToCents for its single rounding step, so any taxed subtotal landing on a half-cent now resolves differently.

nodes.label: invoice-service
nodes.summary: External consumer of roundToCents per the dependency index; will observe the new even-tie rounding directly.

risk.why: External consumer, not modifiable from this repo.

nodes.label: storefront-web
nodes.summary: External consumer of formatCents per the dependency index; displayed totals for half-cent ties will change.

risk.why: External consumer, not modifiable from this repo.

regions.gist: Rounds to whole cents; exact half-cent ties now round to the even cent
Formats an amount as a fixed two-decimal string via roundToCents
Imports roundToCents from the money module
Shape of a line item: price and quantity
Sums price*qty across items, applies tax, rounds once at the end
